Skin Care for Hyderabad Weather: A Routine for Dry Heat, Monsoon and Cool Winters

By Mohammed Nihal, founderPublished 9 November 2026Updated 16 October 20266 min read
Quick answer

Hyderabad's air is drier than coastal cities for much of the year, with very hot summers and cool, dry winters. Skin usually does best with a gentle face wash, a moisturiser on slightly damp skin, a broad-spectrum sunscreen every morning and a little more night cream in winter.

  • Hyderabad sits on the Deccan plateau, so the air is mostly dry
  • Summers (March to May) are very hot
  • Many homes use hard borewell or tanker water
  • Winter mornings are cool and dry

Skin care for Hyderabad weather is mostly about dry heat and strong sun: a gentle face wash, a moisturiser that keeps skin comfortable, a broad-spectrum sunscreen every morning and a simple night cream. Unlike Mumbai or Chennai, Hyderabad sits on the Deccan plateau, so the air is drier for much of the year, summers are very hot and the winter mornings are cool and dry.

The city also brings borewell water in many areas, long bike and cab commutes, dust from construction, and cold AC offices in the IT corridor. Here is one simple routine and how to adjust it through the Hyderabad year.

What Hyderabad weather does to your skin, season by season

Months (roughly)WeatherWhat skin usually feels likeSmall change that helps
March to MayVery hot, mostly dry, harsh afternoon sunTan on face, neck and arms, tight skin after washing, sweat on the foreheadSunscreen reapplied, light moisturiser, avoid very hot water
June to SeptemberMonsoon, warmer and more humid, rain in spellsOilier T-zone, small bumps, damp skin after getting wetLighter textures, dry skin fully after rain, fewer products
October to NovemberPost-monsoon, pleasant days, air starts drying outSkin balances out; cheeks begin to feel tight in the eveningKeep sunscreen; a little more night cream on dry areas
December to FebruaryCool, dry mornings and nights, sunny afternoonsDry patches, rough cheeks, cracked lips and heelsRicher night cream, lukewarm baths, moisturise right after washing

Because the air is drier than in coastal cities, many people in Hyderabad need a little more moisture than they expect, even if their T-zone gets oily. Our guide to night cream for dehydrated skin explains how skin can be oily and thirsty at the same time.

Sunscreen for Hyderabad sun

Hyderabad gets strong sun for most of the year, and summer afternoons are harsh. Daily sunscreen is the single most useful step for a more even-looking skin tone over time.

  • Use a broad-spectrum SPF 30 or higher as the last morning step, about two finger-lengths for face and neck.
  • Reapply before going out again after lunch, and after wiping a sweaty face.
  • Cover the neck, ears and the backs of the hands on long rides.
  • Keep outdoor plans for the morning or evening in April and May where you can.

If you come home with hot, tight skin after a long day out, our after-sun skincare guide shows what to do that evening.

A simple daily routine for Hyderabad skin

Morning

  1. Gentle face wash with cool or lukewarm water. No scrubbing.
  2. A pea-sized amount of moisturiser on slightly damp skin. Our Avocado Glow Cream 15 g (₹399) has only avocado and aloe vera, with no kojic acid, so it works well under sunscreen.
  3. Sunscreen, every day.

Night

  1. Cleanse properly to remove dust, sweat and sunscreen. Cleanse twice if you wore makeup; see how to remove makeup before bed.
  2. Night cream: a pea-sized amount for normal and dry skin, half that for oily skin in the monsoon. Our Avocado Night Cream (30 g, ₹649) has avocado, aloe vera, vitamin B3 and kojic acid; if you use it, wear sunscreen every morning.
  3. In winter, add a little extra cream on dry cheeks and around the nose instead of switching to a heavy oil.

Patch test any new cream on the jawline for a few nights first; our patch test guide explains how. You can compare all options on the night creams page.

Borewell and hard water

Many homes and apartments in Hyderabad use borewell or tanker water, which is often hard. Hard water can leave a film on the skin and make it feel tight or rough after washing.

  • Use a gentle, non-foaming or mild face wash and do not wash your face more than twice a day.
  • Pat dry and moisturise within a minute or two of washing.
  • If your skin feels very tight, try a final splash of filtered or RO water on the face.

Our hard water skin care guide has the full routine.

Bikes, traffic and dust

Long two-wheeler rides in heat and dust are part of daily life for many people here. Dust, sweat and sun together leave skin dull-looking and tanned, especially on the cheeks, nose and neck.

  • Apply sunscreen before the ride and cover your face with a clean cotton cloth or scarf.
  • Wash the cloth often; a dirty mask or helmet pad can cause bumps on the chin and forehead.
  • Rinse your face with plain water when you reach the office if it feels gritty, then moisturise lightly.

Our skincare for bike riders guide goes deeper on helmets and commute care.

IT offices and long AC hours

A day that starts with a hot ride and ends with eight or more hours under cold AC is common in Hitec City, Gachibowli and other office areas. AC dries the air further, so cheeks feel tight by evening. Keep a small desk kit: a light moisturiser for dry areas, sunscreen for the ride home, lip balm and a water bottle. Our AC dry skin routine explains how to manage long office hours.

Hyderabad winter: dry mornings

From about December to February, mornings and nights are cool and dry while afternoons stay sunny. This is when dry patches, cracked lips and rough heels show up.

  • Bathe with lukewarm water; very hot water strips skin.
  • Moisturise face and body right after bathing, while skin is still slightly damp.
  • Do not skip sunscreen just because it feels cool; the afternoon sun is still strong.

Our winter skincare routine for India and dry patches on face guides cover this in more detail. For another plateau city with a similar feel, see skin care for Bangalore weather.

Short answers

Which moisturiser is best for Hyderabad weather? A light cream that absorbs well suits most of the year; in the dry winter months, a slightly richer night cream on the cheeks usually feels better.

Is Hyderabad weather dry or humid? Mostly dry, apart from the monsoon months. That is why skin can feel tight here even if it gets oily on the forehead and nose.

Do I need sunscreen every day in Hyderabad? Yes. The sun is strong for most of the year, so use a broad-spectrum SPF 30 or higher every morning and reapply when you go out again.

Does borewell water affect skin? Hard borewell water can leave skin feeling tight or rough. A gentle face wash, quick moisturising and a final rinse with filtered water can help.

How do I protect my face on a bike in Hyderabad? Wear sunscreen, cover your face with a clean cotton cloth, wash the cloth and helmet pads often and cleanse properly at night.

This is general skincare information, not medical advice. Patch test any new product, and see a dermatologist if you have a skin condition.
